summary: This diff adds a shared auditor_engine_events.py library implementing the AUDITOR_ENGINE_EVENT_SCHEMA (real jsonschema validation, a new append-only audit_events sqlite table, and OpenTelemetry spans with correct parent/child trace-context propagation via reconstructed SpanContext, falling back to a local JSONL exporter rather than an always-on network listener), wires it into all 10 existing audit_pipeline_*.py scripts to populate the previously-always-null event_id column on genuinely-new findings only (verified idempotent: existing findings' event_id is preserved from prior rows, not re-emitted), fixes a real pre-existing bug in the event schema itself (domain's type didn't allow null despite its own enum/description listing it), and authors (but does not execute) a pgaudit-enablement SQL migration for the two live Supabase projects, correctly gated behind a new OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED entry consistent with this repo's established production-infrastructure sign-off convention. I traced the write-lock usage across every modified pipeline and confirmed no lock-nesting/deadlock risk: start_audit_run/complete_audit_run always acquire and release the shared flock outside of each caller's own `with _write_lock()` block, and stamp_new_finding_events reuses the caller's already-open connection rather than re-acquiring the lock. The diff does not touch .github/workflows/** so the hard rule on workflow-file changes does not apply. The one real weakness: none of the 10 pipeline scripts wrap their new `_events.*` calls in any try/except, and the library itself does not catch its own jsonschema.validate() or sqlite errors, so a schema violation (e.g. an out-of-enum --repo value, since --repo has no argparse `choices` constraint) or any other event-emission fault will now raise uncaught and crash the entire audit-finding pipeline run, making a secondary observability feature a new single point of failure for the primary finding-collection function. This is a legitimate robustness gap worth fixing but not a security vulnerability, and given the tier2 classification already mandates human sign-off before merge regardless of this verdict, it does not need to block that review.
issues: No exception handling anywhere around the new auditor_engine_events calls (start_audit_run/stamp_new_finding_events/complete_audit_run) in any of the 10 audit_pipeline_*.py scripts, and the library's own validate_event()/_persist_event() do not catch jsonschema/sqlite errors either -- an event-emission fault (e.g. an out-of-enum --repo string, since --repo has no argparse `choices` restriction matching the schema's repo enum) will crash the entire audit pipeline run instead of degrading gracefully, turning observability into a availability risk for the primary findings-collection function.
